project: Pointed Order Zeta: Artin–Kummer Spectra of Reduction Orders
frozen_definitions: Initial base a is a nonzero integer, a != ±1, initially not a perfect power.
For primes p not dividing a, ord_p(a) is the multiplicative order of a modulo p.
Residual index: I_a(p) = (p - 1) / ord_p(a) = [F_p^x : <a mod p>].
Starting Euler product: Z_a(s,z) = product_{p not dividing a} (1 - I_a(p)^(-z) p^(-s))^(-1).
Initial rigorous domain: real z >= 0 and Re(s) > 1; no analytic continuation is assumed.
Provisional spectrum: Delta_a(z) = lim_{x->infinity} (1/pi(x)) sum_{p<=x, p not dividing a} I_a(p)^(-z), whenever the limit exists.
Kummer fields for the derivation target: K_n(a) = Q(zeta_n, a^(1/n)), subject to perfect-power and entanglement caveats.
foundational_results: For p not dividing a, ord_p(a) divides p-1 and I_a(p) is [F_p^x:<a>].
For n >= 1 and p not dividing a: n | I_a(p) iff n | (p-1) and a mod p is an n-th power in F_p^x.
For fixed n and p not dividing a*n: n | I_a(p) iff p splits completely in K_n(a)=Q(zeta_n,a^(1/n)).
The non-perfect-power hypothesis is not needed for the fixed-n splitting equivalence; it matters for degree formulas and later constants.
For fixed n, Chebotarev gives density 1/[K_n(a):Q] for n | I_a(p), up to a finite exceptional set.
For any arithmetic f, f(I_a(p)) = sum_{n | I_a(p)} (mu*f)(n), pointwise finitely.
For f_z(n)=n^(-z), g_z=mu*f_z is multiplicative and g_z(q^k)=q^(-kz)-q^(-(k-1)z).
For z=0, g_0 is epsilon; for fixed n, g_z(n) tends to mu(n) as z tends to +infinity.
For z >= 0 and Re(s)>1, the Euler product and logarithmic double series are absolutely controlled by zeta(Re(s)).
prior_art_results: Residual index i_a(p) is standard terminology; the fixed exact-index problem I_a(p)=t is the near-primitive-root problem.
Felix-Murty (2012), Lemma 2.1, records the fixed-n splitting criterion as classical: d | i_a(p) iff p splits completely in Q(zeta_d,a^(1/d)), away from the usual exceptional primes.
Felix-Murty (2012), Theorem 1.7, gives under GRH fixed-base asymptotics for a broad class of f(i_a(p)) and identifies the constant as sum_d g(d)/[Q(zeta_d,a^(1/d)):Q], where f=1*g.

For each fixed real z>0, Session-2 gives |g_z(n)|<=1, so Felix-Murty Theorem 1.7 immediately yields the proposed Delta_a(z) and its Kummer-degree series under GRH in the paper's standing positive-base setup. The negative-base extension of this general weighted theorem was not independently source-matched in Session 3.

Wagstaff's exact degree formula, reproduced in Felix-Murty Proposition 3.3, gives [Q(zeta_n,a^(1/n)):Q] asymptotic_a n*phi(n), including explicit perfect-power, sign, discriminant, and 2-adic corrections.
Consequently sum_n |g_z(n)|/[K_n(a):Q] converges absolutely for every fixed real z>0; the prime-average interchange still requires effective uniformity and is supplied conditionally by Felix-Murty.

Akbary-Fakhari (2024) explicitly formulates the same generalized-Artin Kummer-degree constant and gives product/character-sum expressions for multiplicative weights, including g_z once convergence is checked.

Lenstra-Moree-Stevenhagen (2014) identifies entanglement with dependencies among local splitting fields and associated correction factors; it does not alter the individual fixed-n splitting criterion.

No direct primary source was located for the exact two-variable product Z_a(s,z); finite-Galois Frobenian/Chebotarev Euler-product theory is adjacent but does not literally contain the infinite-Kummer weight I_a(p)^(-z).

The leading real s->1+ logarithmic coefficient is largely packaging once the Felix-Murty weighted prime asymptotic is taken as input; stronger continuation, nonvanishing, complex-z dependence, and Kummer-tower L-factorization remain possible questions.
open_questions: Does Felix-Murty Theorem 1.7, or a later theorem of equal generality, explicitly cover negative integer bases a for general f(i_a(p))? The degree and exact-index machinery do cover negative a, but the weighted theorem's negative-base hypothesis should be source-matched before use.
Does the normalized infinite-Kummer Euler product H_a(s,z)=Z_a(s,z) zeta(s)^(-Delta_a(z)) admit a holomorphic and nonvanishing continuation beyond Re(s)>1 for fixed z?
What is the best half-plane of continuation for H_a(s,z), conditionally or unconditionally?
Can Z_a(s,z) or H_a(s,z) be expressed as a convergent product/quotient of Dedekind or Artin L-functions attached to the Kummer tower?
For which complex z can Delta_a(z), Z_a(s,z), and any normalized factor be treated uniformly or holomorphically?
Does an infinite-tower L-factorization introduce natural boundaries or secondary singularities not visible from the mean value alone?
Is the frozen local factor (1-I_a(p)^(-z)p^(-s))^(-1) analytically useful enough to justify retaining Z_a(s,z), or should a logarithmic derivative or another transform replace it?
What parts, if any, of a pointed algebraic-group or 1-motive generalization remain nontrivial after the G_m generalized-Artin collision?
killed_conjectures: Naive shorthand: a mod p is an n-th power iff n divides I_a(p), without also requiring n divides p-1. This is false when n does not divide p-1.
Candidate novelty of the fixed-n Kummer splitting mechanism: it is classical generalized-Artin machinery.
Candidate novelty of the general Mobius/Kummer mean-value constant: Felix-Murty proves this framework, and Akbary-Fakhari explicitly develops the corresponding constants.
Candidate novelty of Delta_a(z) for fixed real z>0 as a new residual-index mean: it is an immediate specialization of Felix-Murty Theorem 1.7 under GRH.

Candidate novelty of the word 'spectrum' at the G_m mean-value level: the object is more naturally a Dirichlet/Mellin transform of the residual-index distribution, equivalently a Laplace transform of log I_a(p).
surviving_conjectures: Potential reframed target only: the normalized infinite-Kummer weighted Euler product may possess analytic continuation, nonvanishing, complex-z structure, or an L-function factorization not automatic from known generalized-Artin mean-value results. No novelty claim is made.
